title: Internal dashboard visualization guidelines for unit economics metrics
creator: Alicia Perez
description:
Problem
The Unit Economics dashboard is going to be used by Finance, Product, and Eng for exec reporting and day-to-day diagnosis. Cost metrics are easy to misread (especially when small changes look “big” due to axis scaling, rounding, or incomplete coverage). We need shared presentation rules so the UI communicates: (1) the correct units and magnitude, (2) what is comparable vs not, and (3) how trustworthy the number is right now.

Scope
These are UI/visualization guidelines for the internal Console page (DES-311/DES-312) and any derivative screenshots used in KPI decks. This is NOT a definition of the metric itself (see PM-483 + metric dictionary), and it is NOT the data quality spec (see SLO doc). It is about how the dashboard presents the metric to minimize misinterpretation.

Primary metric(s)
- Blended $/1M output tokens (time series + breakdown tables)
- Secondary: cache hit rate, batching efficiency, avg output length, streaming share, quantization profile distribution

Principles
1) Prefer clarity over precision. Cost numbers are estimates with known caveats; show enough precision to compare meaningfully, but not so much that people infer false accuracy.
2) Always include context. Every chart/table should make the unit and the dimension explicit (“$/1M output tokens — model: X — region: Y — tier: Z”).
3) Show confidence, not just values. When coverage is partial or freshness is behind, the UI must communicate this prominently.
4) Avoid visual tricks. No truncated axes on $ metrics; don’t let color imply “good/bad” when it’s actually “high/low.”

Formatting + units (canonical)
A) Currency
- Use “$” prefix for all cost metrics.
- Use USD throughout v1. Do not add currency toggles (non-goal).
- If a view is not USD (e.g., future), the currency must be included in the label itself, not only a tooltip.

B) Primary unit: “$/1M output tokens”
- Always label as “$/1M output tokens” (not “$/M tokens” or “cost per token”).
- Tooltip should include the expanded definition: “Blended infrastructure cost allocated to this slice / total output tokens in this slice * 1,000,000.”
- In tables, the column header should be “$/1M output tokens (blended)” to reinforce blended vs marginal.

C) Rounding + significant digits
- Default display for $/1M output tokens:
  - If value >= $1.00: show 2 decimals (e.g., $12.34)
  - If value < $1.00: show 3 decimals down to $0.001 (e.g., $0.742)
  - Below $0.001: show “< $0.001” (avoid noisy micro-decimals)
- Percent deltas:
  - Show 1 decimal (e.g., +3.2%)
  - If absolute change < 0.1%: show “~0.0%” and rely on sparkline/tooltip
- Token counts:
  - Use compact units: 1.2B, 340M, 12.4M, 980K
  - Always include the raw integer in tooltip

D) Time aggregation labeling
- Time series axis must specify aggregation grain: “Hourly” or “Daily”.
- When the user selects a date range shorter than 48 hours, default to hourly; otherwise daily (unless the user manually overrides).
- Any screenshot used for exec reporting should prefer daily grain unless a known incident/regression is being shown.

Charting rules (time series)
1) Y-axis behavior for $ metrics
- Do not use truncated y-axis for $/1M output tokens.
- If the range is narrow and changes are small, show the narrow range via a secondary visual cue (e.g., “±X% band” in tooltip) rather than cropping the axis.

2) Line + comparison mode
- Single series default: current filters.
- Comparison mode (e.g., previous period) should:
  - Use two lines with consistent colors across the app (Primary = current, Secondary = comparison)
  - Add a small inline legend: “Current” / “Previous period”
  - Include a summary above the chart: “Avg $/1M: $X.XX (Current) vs $Y.YY (Previous), Δ +Z.Z%”

3) Smoothing
- No smoothing by default; it hides spikes that matter for incident response.
- If we add smoothing later, it must be an explicit toggle and the raw series must remain accessible.

4) Outlier communication
- When a spike is detected (or the user hovers), show:
  - Value, delta vs previous point, and supporting signals (cache hit rate, batching efficiency) in tooltip.
  - Avoid auto-annotation unless we have a reliable cause label.

Tables (top-N + breakdowns)
1) Column requirements
- For cost breakdown tables, show these columns in v1:
  - “$/1M output tokens (blended)”
  - “Output tokens”
  - “Allocated cost ($)” (if Finance approves exposure for internal-only)
  - “Coverage” (see confidence indicator) or “Data status”
- Provide tooltips for each metric.

2) Sorting defaults
- Default sort by highest $/1M output tokens (descending) for “Top cost outliers.”
- Provide a toggle to sort by “Output tokens” to avoid focusing on small-volume noise.

3) Min-volume guardrails
- If output tokens for a row < threshold (proposal: < 1M tokens for selected period), show a “Low volume” badge and de-emphasize the row (muted text). Still sortable/filterable.
- Do not hide by default; Finance may still want to see small slices, but we need a clear visual signal.

Color + semantics
- Use Redwood Console standard palette.
- Avoid red/green for cost values (cost high/low isn’t inherently bad without context). Use neutral sequential color scale.
- Use red/yellow only for data quality/confidence issues, not for the metric value itself.

Confidence / Data quality indicator (UI spec)
Goal: A lightweight, always-visible status that tells the user whether to trust the number.

A) Placement
- Show a “Data status” chip near the main metric at the top of the dashboard.
- Also show a per-row status in tables when a slice is affected.

B) States (v1)
- “Good” (green/neutral): freshness within SLO; required dimensions present above threshold; no detected anomalies.
- “Delayed” (yellow): freshness behind (e.g., last complete hour is behind now by > SLO threshold).
- “Partial coverage” (yellow): missing dimension coverage above threshold (e.g., unknown region/tier/model values exceed allowed %).
- “Investigating” (yellow): incident flag set by oncall / known pipeline issue.
- “Unavailable” (red): cannot compute reliably (missing core inputs / metering broken).

C) Copy rules
- Chip label must be short (“Good”, “Partial”, “Delayed”).
- Tooltip must include:
  - “Last complete data: <timestamp>”
  - The reason (freshness / missing dims / anomaly)
  - Link text (internal) to runbook: “How to investigate discrepancies”

D) Avoid “confidence %” in v1
- Do NOT show a numeric confidence score yet; it implies rigor we don’t have and can be gamed. If we add it later, it needs clear computation + Finance/SRE agreement.

Caveats and disclaimers (must show in UI)
- Always include an info box or tooltip near the primary metric:
  - “Blended cost includes allocation and may differ from marginal runtime changes.”
  - “Totals may not match billing for the same window due to reconciliation timing and allocation cadence.”
  - “Use comparison mode and volume context before drawing conclusions.”
- For Dedicated/Private tiers: include a note that allocation may include idle capacity treatment per methodology.

Interaction guidelines
- Filter changes should update the title/subtitle inline. Example:
  - “$/1M output tokens — Feb 1–Feb 7 — All regions — Tier: Hosted (self-serve) — Model: Redwood-Llama-3.1-70B (q4_k_m)”
- Any exported image (copy chart) must include the subtitle with filters and the “Last complete data” timestamp.

Acceptance criteria
- DES-311/DES-312 incorporate the formatting rules for $/1M, percent deltas, and token counts.
- Designs include a Data status chip and a tooltip spec with the required fields.
- No truncated y-axis on $ charts in final UI.
- Finance review confirms copy/disclaimer language is acceptable for internal exec reporting.

Open questions
1) Do we show “Allocated cost ($)” in tables by default, or behind a secondary toggle? (Sensitivity: internal-only but still may be restricted.)
2) What are the exact thresholds for “Low volume” and “Partial coverage”? (Needs SRE + telemetry alignment.)
3) Do we need separate “Finance view” vs “Live view” labels in the UI, or is Data status sufficient?

Links
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/internal-unit-economics-dashboard-prd
- Metric dictionary: confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/unit-economics-dashboard-metrics-and-definitions
- Pipeline SLOs: confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/unit-economics-pipeline-slo
- Wireframes: drive/engineering/console-and-tooling/dashboard-wireframes-v0

Notes
This ticket is intentionally prescriptive because the audience includes execs. If we can’t satisfy a guideline due to data limitations (e.g., missing “last complete data”), we should block launch or gate the view rather than ship ambiguous UI.
comments: 2025-01-13 — Chloe Martin: +1 on no truncated y-axis. For the comparison summary, can we keep it to 1 line max so it doesn’t push content below the fold on smaller screens?

2025-01-14 — Rishi Malhotra: Please keep “blended” in the header. We’ve had recurring confusion between blended vs marginal in other KPI contexts. Also strongly prefer no numeric confidence score in v1.

2025-01-16 — Allison Grant: For Data status states, add a distinct “Investigating” state that can be flipped during incidents; ties nicely to alert routing. We can provide a boolean from the pipeline service for v1 if needed.
2025-01-21 — Felix Schneider: From API side we can provide last_complete_hour and basic coverage ratios (unknown_region_pct, unknown_tier_pct). Need explicit thresholds to map to chip states.
2025-01-24 — Laura Bennett: Disclaimers look good. Make sure any exported screenshot includes the time window + last complete data timestamp; we’ll use these in quarterly KPI pack drafts.

2025-02-03 — Alicia Perez: Updated rounding rules after looking at sample data from the spreadsheet. Added “< $0.001” rule to avoid false precision. Marking ready for implementation in DES-311/DES-312.
2025-02-05 — Marissa Cole: Approved. Please ensure the “Low volume” badge is visible enough; we want to prevent overreacting to tiny slices during dogfood.
